findings.title: Arbitrary foundation family may be used
findings.body: The command selects the first one-level structural-foundation family having writable parameters named Length and Width. In a normal project with multiple qualifying footing or pile-cap families, collector order is not a stable selection rule, so the same CAD input can create the wrong family and then duplicate that wrong type for every detected rectangle. The base family must be selected deterministically, configured, or chosen by the user.

findings.title: Loop traversal continues after closing a polygon
findings.body: BuildLoops does not stop once currentEnd returns to the starting point. If another line on S-FND touches that vertex, the greedy search appends it and continues traversing, so valid rectangles that share a vertex or have connected auxiliary linework are merged and subsequently rejected or misinterpreted. Closure should finalize the current loop before considering other incident lines.

findings.title: Non-horizontal CAD rectangles are accepted with incorrect geometry
findings.body: The parser calculates minZ and maxZ but never validates them. An orthogonal 3D rectangle whose longest edge is horizontal can therefore pass, while width is computed from its XY projection and center Z is copied from only the first point. This creates a foundation with incorrect size and location. The parser should reject non-planar/non-horizontal loops or deliberately project them using a documented rule.

findings.title: Missing level is passed to family creation
findings.body: The fallback level lookup can still return null, but the command proceeds to NewFamilyInstance with that null level. Models without an available Level consequently fail only after type duplication and placement processing begins, producing an opaque exception instead of a controlled validation failure. The resolved level should be checked before entering the placement loop.
